source.title: Improving Visual Prompt Tuning by Gaussian Neighborhood Minimization for Long-Tailed Visual Recognition
source.authors: Meng-Ke Li; Ye Liu; Yang Lu; Yi-Qun Zhang; Yiu-Ming Cheung; Hui Huang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses flat-minima optimization as a way to improve generalization and reports its proposed method’s held-out classification results. It does not test any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out accuracy comparisons for GNM, SAM, and baseline training. These bear on generalization but do not measure the specific behaviors or properties named in V1–V8. Other cited optimizer results are prior work, not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flat-minima generalization premise to develop GNM and evaluates its classification accuracy and computation time. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship: the landscapes are visual comparisons, without measured gaps, matched training losses, or rankings against other generalization measures. Its other experiments do not test V1–V6 or V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: GNM-PT improves long-tailed recognition and aims to balance head- and tail-class generalization, while classifier rebalancing can sacrifice head-class accuracy. Computational savings are relative to SAM: Table 4 shows GNM takes slightly longer per epoch than baseline training.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes a pre-trained ViT with VPT on long-tailed data, using GNM and DRW; it does not use the original methods specified by the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: On CIFAR100-LT at imbalance ratio 100, reported accuracy differs by loss and optimizer; the paper also reports different effects across head, medium, and tail classes, and across classifier-rebalancing settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR100-LT at imbalance ratio 100, GNM increases CE accuracy from 81.02% to 82.50% and GCL+DRW accuracy from 89.58% to 90.28%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GNM improves held-out classification accuracy in the tested visual prompt tuning setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 1, 4, and 6 visually associate flatter loss landscapes with improved classification accuracy, without measuring magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GNM can produce visually flatter loss landscapes alongside improved held-out accuracy in the tested settings.

record.problems: The reported accuracy comparisons do not report train-to-test gaps. No uncertainty estimates are given for these results. The paper’s landscape comparison is visual, and the reported setup is a pre-trained prompt-tuned model on long-tailed data.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure 3 gives class-split accuracy comparisons, but values are figure-only; its textual description says GNM improves performance across all categories and SAM declines GCL tail-class performance. These outcomes are not mapped to V1–V8, so they are not included as version rows.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and random-label training, memorization capacity, and held-out accuracy relative to chance.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets; SAM and GNM comparisons do not test this distinction.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout effects across data sizes and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus measured training-to-test gaps among comparably fitted networks, including rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdicts are warranted. The supplied text, including the appendices, provides no additional results testing V1–V8. The correctly transcribed Table 4 accuracies can be retained as method-performance findings outside the claim-evidence rows.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error across widths beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness compared with training-to-test gaps and other measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
